breaks.quote: If the answer is no, prune. Pick something that still matters to you and prune it.
breaks.why: The reader is asked to end something they value, but the reasons (lost hours, full months, room regained) were only told inside the author's own story and never argued in the reader's life.

breaks.quote: The hours were only part of the cost. Little by little, my list had crept to the point that every month was filled with the same things
breaks.why: The cost of the reader's current way gets one or two sentences inside the story, so the reason is named, not argued.

breaks.quote: Yours might hold a weekly class you joined two years ago, a group chat you read every night
breaks.why: The reader's own list is one short paragraph just before the ask, so the case for pruning is squeezed in at the last moment.
